passage: Rain forced the whole school into the noisy canteen on Manoj's first day in Nagpur. Steel plates clattered, and every bench was full of loud groups. Manoj held his tiffin tightly and stood by the door, his ears hot. Nobody looked up. He walked to the end of a bench and smiled at a boy with a ball-shaped eraser. "Can I sit here?" The boy, Siddharth, nodded without much talk. They ate quietly. Later Manoj heard Siddharth's group planning a card game and asked, "Can I play?" "Next time," one of them said. Manoj went home tired, but he told himself one lunch was only the start.

qa.q: Why was the school crowded into the canteen on Manoj's first day?
qa.a: Rain forced the whole school into the noisy canteen.

qa.q: What was Manoj feeling as he stood by the door with his tiffin?
qa.a: Lonely and unsure: he held his tiffin tightly and his ears were hot.

qa.q: What small step could Manoj try next?
qa.a: Sit near Siddharth again, smile, and ask to join a game.

qa.q: How might Siddharth see the new boy?
qa.a: Siddharth nodded without much talk, so he may be a bit shy himself, but he was willing to share a bench.

grounding: On his first day nobody talks to the new child at lunch; he tries small steps like smiling, sitting near someone and asking to join, and tells himself it is a start.

passage: The canteen at Tanvir's new school was louder than a railway station. He carried his tiffin past table after table where everyone already had a place. He sat at the very end of one bench and ate his parathas slowly, pretending to read the menu board. His throat felt tight. Nobody looked up. After lunch, a group ran out to play kho-kho. Tanvir's feet wanted to go back to class. Instead he walked to the edge of the ground and smiled at a girl tying her laces. 'Can I play?' Deepika shrugged. 'We need one more on our side anyway.' He was caught in the first minute. But on the way back, Deepika said, 'You run fast. Sit with us tomorrow?'

qa.q: What game did the group play after lunch?
How did Tanvir feel eating at the end of the bench?
qa.a: Lonely and nervous; his throat felt tight, and he pretended to read the menu so nobody would notice.
Smiling at someone and asking to join the game, instead of going back to class alone.

qa.q: How might Deepika see the new boy?
qa.a: As a newcomer who runs fast; she is easygoing about it and invites him to sit with them.

grounding: A new boy eats lunch alone on his first day, then takes a small step and asks to join a game.

passage:
Monday. Lalit's first day at the new school in Bhopal. At lunch he sat under the neem tree with his dabba and watched the others laugh in groups. Nobody came over. At home he told Papa, 'It's the worst.' Papa said, 'First days usually are.'
Thursday. Lalit tried one thing. He sat on the bench beside Aditi, who was reading a comic, and asked, 'Is that the one with the flying cow?' She laughed and showed him. They didn't talk much after that, but it was something.
Three weeks later. Aditi saved him a seat, and two boys from the back row asked Lalit to join their cricket at break. He still missed his old gang, but lunch no longer felt like the longest part of the day.

qa.q: Where did Lalit sit at lunch on his first day?
qa.a: Under the neem tree with his dabba.

qa.q: What was Lalit feeling on Monday evening when he spoke to Papa?
qa.a: Lonely and discouraged; he called the day the worst.

qa.q: What step did Lalit try on Thursday?
qa.a: Sitting beside Aditi and asking about her comic, a small way to start talking.

qa.q: How might Aditi see Lalit's question about the comic?
qa.a: As a friendly opening; she laughed and showed him, and weeks later she saved him a seat.

grounding: Over three weeks a lonely new boy takes small steps at lunch and slowly makes friends.
